answer.location_description: A full-width periodic horizontal stripe (grating) pattern covering essentially the whole crop, from about row 2 to row 23 and all columns. The stripes have a period of about 4 rows: rows 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 are weighted as bright bands, and rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 as dark bands.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe / line-grating artifact (non-anatomical texture)
answer.mechanism: The structured first-layer units fall into two anti-phase groups. Group B (units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27, 28; negative biases) has positive weights on the bands at rows 4-5, 8-9, 16-17 and 20-21, and on rows 12-13 at the image edges. It has negative weights on rows 2-3, 18-19, 22-23, rows 14-15 at the edges, and rows 6-7 on the right. These band weights run across the full width, including the corner columns 0-3 and 20-23, far from the nodule. Group B feeds layer-2 units u1 (out +99), u8 (+58) and u0 (+66). Examples: u1 receives 3:+70, 21:+72, 24:+66, 27:+77, 28:+94; u8 receives 3:+91, 8:+92, 24:+93. Group B therefore pushes the logit toward malignant. Group A (units 2, 5, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 25, 29, 30; large positive biases) carries exactly the opposite stripe phase. It feeds u9 (out -72) and u11 (out -64), for example u11 receives 14:+99, 18:+96, 25:+94, 29:+87, 30:+87. Group A also inhibits u1 (25:-86, 30:-75). So the stripe phase present in the image is read out directly as malignant versus benign.
answer.evidence: Unit 24, edge columns 0-3, row by row: r2 -7 7 -11 -17; r4 9 5 -5 37; r5 -6 42 46 45; r8 34 48 46 46; r14 5 -14 -13 -37; r15 2 -16 -15 -21; r20 41 44 25 34; r21 23 14 55 35. Unit 3 shows the same pattern: r2-3 about -20 to -47 across all columns; r4-5 about +20 to +43 across all columns; r15 cols 0-4 -17 -25 -36 -34 -33; r20-21 about +20 to +45; r22-23 slightly negative. Unit 14 shows the inverse: r2-3 about +30 to +60 across the full width; r8 cols 7-15 about -28 to -70; r14-15 cols 0-4 +19 to +64; r18-19 about +25 to +60; r20 slightly negative; r22-23 positive. The same alternating 2-row-on / 2-row-off structure repeats in all ~16 structured units, at full width and with about the same magnitude in the corners as near the centre. This is inconsistent with a roughly circular nodule centred at rows 10-13. Units 0, 1, 4, 6, 7, 9-13, 15, 22, 23, 26 and 31 look like unstructured noise.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size and extent around the centre. Benign-voting units (2, 14, 25, 29, etc.) like a small bright core at rows 10-13, cols 10-13, with a dark ring around it. Malignant-voting units (3, 8, 24, 27, 28) are inhibited at the core and excited by a bright annulus of radius about 3-6 px, so a larger nodule extending beyond the core pushes toward malignant.
